executionType: independent manual black-box and source review suite
commonSetup: Fresh browser context, synthetic values, other required fields valid according to disclosed policy; use not_scorable for absent requirement or blocked for missing prerequisite.

cases.procedure: Open the form through public UI. Inventory visible date, time, and location/timezone input concepts.
cases.expected: The requested input concepts are present and usable. Additional chart fields are not mandated without a calculation contract.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Start with an empty form and attempt submission.
cases.expected: Missing required values produce actionable feedback; the form does not report successful validation.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Omit each field the implementation declares required, one at a time, keeping the others synthetically valid.
cases.expected: Each missing required value is identified with understandable feedback.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Correct an invalid field and retry.
cases.expected: The corrected field is not still described as invalid when the supplied value is valid under the disclosed policy.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Supply a complete synthetic valid input under the implementation's disclosed rules; observe submission.
cases.expected: No erroneous validation rejection. Exact success UI or server behavior is not scorable without a specified submission contract.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Attempt an impossible date such as 2024-02-30 using the available controls.
cases.expected: The impossible date cannot be accepted as a valid calendar date. Prevention by a native widget is acceptable; separately review validation tests.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Attempt 2023-02-29 in a Gregorian input mode.
cases.expected: The non-leap-year date is not accepted as a valid Gregorian date. If the mode is not Gregorian, report not scorable rather than assume a calendar.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Enter 2024-02-29 in a Gregorian input mode.
cases.expected: The date is calendar-valid; rejection solely as an impossible Gregorian date fails. Unspecified product date ranges are evaluated separately.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Review and exercise declared lower/upper date boundaries, if any, and adjacent values.
cases.expected: Boundary behavior matches disclosed policy. Whether the chosen product bounds are correct is not scorable because none are specified.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Attempt hour 24 or minute 60, using the applicable time representation.
cases.expected: Impossible time values are prevented or rejected; no silent normalization to a different birth time.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Try 00:00 and 23:59 in a 24-hour mode, or their equivalent in the chosen representation.
cases.expected: Both are valid time-of-day values; exact product restrictions are not specified.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: If a location field is available, enter an unsupported or nonsensical location; record any declared supported set.
cases.expected: Location acceptance/rejection must be described. Exact supported set and resolution rules are not defined, so correctness of those policy choices is not scorable.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: If an IANA timezone input is provided, try Not/A_Zone, then America/Los_Angeles.
cases.expected: If the implementation promises IANA validation, the first is rejected and the second recognized. Which timezone representation is required remains unspecified.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Inspect handling of 2024-03-10 02:30 and 2024-11-03 01:30 in America/Los_Angeles if timezone resolution is implemented.
cases.expected: No expected disambiguation or rejection policy is specified. Record behavior as not scorable; do not invent an oracle.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Inspect accessible names for every required control using the browser accessibility tree.
cases.expected: Every required control has a meaningful accessible label; placeholder-only or visually adjacent unassociated text is insufficient.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Complete and submit using Tab, Shift+Tab, arrow keys as appropriate, and Enter/Space without a pointer.
cases.expected: All relevant controls and submission are operable by keyboard with a visible focus indicator and no trap.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Trigger errors; inspect control association, accessible descriptions, and feedback discoverability.
cases.expected: Errors are understandable and programmatically associated with relevant controls or exposed through accessible native validation; color alone is insufficient.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Trigger submission errors and observe focus order and the next keyboard action.
cases.expected: Focus remains predictable and errors can be found and corrected. No exact autofocus target is mandated.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Inspect semantic markup and reflow at 1280x800 and 390x844.
cases.expected: Form semantics support assistive technology; essential fields and errors remain readable and usable at both viewports. This is not a full WCAG audit.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Use synthetic sentinel values; inspect browser console, captured server output, source logging calls, and URLs.
cases.expected: No birth inputs are logged or placed in URLs. Inspect source as well as observed output; absence in one run alone is not exhaustive evidence.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Inspect cookies, local/session storage, network activity, and persistence code before and after entry/submission.
cases.expected: No unsupported storage or external transmission of birth information; distinguish normal static asset requests from input-bearing requests.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Review fields collected and changed files.
cases.expected: No real personal data, credentials, or unnecessary personal fields are introduced; additional required chart fields need a documented basis.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Run the five frozen npm commands; inspect implementation-authored validation tests and their discovered file set.
cases.expected: Commands pass and meaningful validation tests are actually executed, including missing/invalid cases and fixed expected outcomes.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md

cases.procedure: Review diff for TypeScript safety, focused components, validation separation, maintainability, unnecessary complexity, and architecture consistency.
cases.expected: Use the evidence-backed rubric in evaluation-plan.md; do not score compliance with treatment wording itself.
cases.source: Issue #3 acceptance criteria; baseline product-requirements.md and architecture.md
